correctness.rationale: For every r,m>=2, graph automorphism averaging preserves feasibility and cannot increase the convex operator-norm SLEM. The invariant spectrum is exactly 1, 1-ra (mult m-1), 1-ma-rb (mult r-1), 1-(m+r)a; its first and last nonconstant modes yield a unique optimal a subject to capacity. Solving the remaining two-sided scalar constraint gives the stated complete nonempty interval for b and verifies equality. Averaging a general optimum and using nonnegativity establishes sharp mandatory/optional/forbidden core-edge use. Exact rational testing covered 561 parameter pairs/1683 endpoint and midpoint instances; separate LP comparison 209 cases; dense eigenspectra 77 cases. Finite computation is supplementary and not an infinite proof. No unsupported uniqueness statement is made.

value.rationale: The natural two-parameter family K_r join independent_m models a clique of mutually communicating agents joined to many independent clients. It has two exact, structural, sharp design thresholds: core links are compulsory for m<r, optional for r<=m<2r and necessarily assigned zero optimal probability for m>=2r. For any fixed m>=2 as r grows, the optimum SLEM on the full split graph tends to zero, while the established optimum on its complete-bipartite spanning subgraph tends to one, so the core-edge effect is qualitative rather than a routine small gain. A complete invariant-optimizer interval and exact uniform-stationary spectral rates for all r,m are directly usable design facts; no downstream theorem is claimed.
